faqs.a: X always moves first — that is the standard rule everywhere, and this game follows it. Going first is a real advantage: with perfect play X can force at least a draw, while O can only force a draw if X makes a mistake.
faqs.q: Who goes first in Tic Tac Toe?

faqs.a: No. The hard mode uses the minimax algorithm, which evaluates every possible continuation of the game and picks a move that guarantees at least a draw. The best result a human can achieve against perfect play is a draw. If you want wins, switch to easy mode, where the computer picks randomly.
faqs.q: Can the hard computer be beaten?

faqs.a: When all 9 squares are filled and none of the 8 winning lines holds three identical marks, nobody can win, so the game is a draw. Draws are common between careful players — in fact, perfect play from both sides always draws.
faqs.q: Why did my game end in a draw?

faqs.a: Easy mode picks a completely random empty square on every turn. It does not block your threats or build its own lines, so it is genuinely beatable and good for kids or casual play.
faqs.q: How does the easy computer work?

faqs.a: Take the center square if it is free — it belongs to 4 winning lines, more than any corner (3) or edge (2). Always block an immediate threat (two enemy marks with an empty third square). Then build forks: two threats at once, which cannot both be blocked.
faqs.q: What is the best strategy to win?

tic-tac-toe.formula:
Win check — any of these 8 lines all holding the same mark wins:
Rows: (1,2,3), (4,5,6), (7,8,9) | Columns: (1,4,7), (2,5,8), (3,6,9) | Diagonals: (1,5,9), (3,5,7).
Hard AI (minimax): every reachable board is scored — +10 for an O win, -10 for an X win, 0 for a draw, adjusted by depth so faster wins rank higher. The AI chooses the move with the highest guaranteed score, so it never loses.

howTo: Pick your mode: Two Players (a friend on the same screen), Easy (a relaxed computer), or Hard (an unbeatable computer).
X always starts. Tap any empty square to place your mark.
Players alternate turns. Watch for the winning line to light up when someone gets three in a row.
Press New Round to play again — your score is kept. Press Reset Scores to start the tally from zero.
On hard mode, try to force a draw: take the center if it is free, and always block an immediate threat.
keyFacts: Tic Tac Toe is played on a 3x3 grid with two marks: X and O. X always makes the first move.
You win by placing three of your marks in a straight line — any row, any column, or either diagonal.
There are 8 possible winning lines on the board: 3 rows, 3 columns, and 2 diagonals.
If all 9 squares fill up with no winning line, the game ends in a draw.
Perfect play from both sides always ends in a draw — the game is mathematically solved.
The hard computer on this page uses the minimax algorithm, which examines every possible future board and can never be beaten.

Moves: X plays square 1, O plays 5, X plays 2, O plays 9, X plays 3.
1. The top row now reads X, X, X in squares 1, 2, 3.
2. The win check tests line (1,2,3): all three hold X. X wins.
3. The hard AI avoids this trap: after X takes 1 and 2, minimax scores every reply, sees that only square 3 stops the forced loss, and blocks there — which is why hard mode never loses.
